title: Choosing the Right Control
context: You are the security lead at an SMB. Three situations arrive simultaneously. At each step, choose the response that best aligns with the framework.

n1.text: An employee attempts to access financial data they are not authorized to view. What do you implement as a priority?

choices.text: A warning banner on the workstation
choices.why: A banner is a deterrent, but it does not prevent access.

choices.text: Least privilege and role-based access control
choices.why: Least privilege prevents unauthorized access upfront: it is a preventive technical control.
A log review is detective: it identifies what happened, but does not prevent it.

n2.text: Legal requires that administrator actions cannot be denied. Which security property are you targeting?

choices.why: Availability concerns access to the service, not proof of the action.
Non-repudiation ensures an action cannot be denied, through logging and digital signatures.
Integrity protects against modification, but does not provide proof of origin.

n3.text: An incident reveals that the existing SIEM does not cover endpoints. You deploy an EDR in the meantime. How do you classify this control?

choices.text: Compensating: it partially covers a missing control
choices.why: A compensating control bridges a temporary coverage gap.
An EDR is a technical control, not a written policy or rule.

choices.text: Physical: it acts on the environment
choices.why: EDR is a technical/logical control on the endpoint.

n4.outcome: You distinguished preventive, non-repudiation, and compensating controls — the three key reflexes expected for objective 1.1.

debrief: Least privilege is a preventive technical control.
Non-repudiation is achieved through reliable logging and digital signatures, not encryption alone.
A compensating control temporarily covers a gap.
